intro: The course's Cast of Characters: 39 figures from the anti-Castro, intelligence and organized-crime worlds that the alternative theories turn on. Summaries are in our own words. Where the source document asserts someone's involvement in the assassination, that is marked as its claim, not established fact. Page numbers refer to the Cast of Characters PDF.

people.name: John Martino
people.summary: In 1964 promoted the story that Castro had Kennedy killed in retaliation for U.S. plots, with Oswald recruited by Cuban intelligence. He reportedly told a friend and his wife he had been a courier carrying money for the plot, and before his death in 1975 told reporter John Cummings his Oswald stories were false and that two Cuban exiles (believed to be Herminio Díaz García and Virgilio González) were the gunmen.

people.name: Eugenio Martínez
people.summary: Cuban-born Miami exile who took part in Operation Tilt and was one of the five men recruited by G. Gordon Liddy and E. Howard Hunt for the 1972 Watergate burglary.

people.name: Eddie Bayo
people.summary: Claimed in 1962 that two Soviet officers in Cuba wanted to defect with information on missiles left after the Missile Crisis. His story led to Operation Tilt, a failed 1963 raid to bring them out. He stayed behind in Cuba and is rumored to have been captured and executed.

people.name: Sylvia Odio
people.summary: Daughter of a jailed opponent of Castro. Testified that in late September 1963 two Latin men claiming to be from the exile group JURE visited her Dallas apartment with an American introduced as "Leon," whom she later identified as Oswald. If true, it ties Oswald to anti-Castro militants rather than the leftist portrait in the Warren Report.

people.name: David Sánchez Morales
people.summary: CIA operations officer under military cover; in Cuba from 1958, involved in the Bay of Pigs and (per CIA officer Tom Clines) the capture of Che Guevara. A friend, Ruben Carbajal, quoted him blaming Kennedy for the Bay of Pigs deaths and boasting that "we took care of" him. Some researchers place him at the Ambassador Hotel the night Robert Kennedy was shot.

people.name: William "Rip" Robertson
people.summary: WWII Marine, then CIA. Took part in the 1954 Guatemala operation, landed with Brigade 2506 at the Bay of Pigs against orders, then worked at the JM/WAVE station in Miami under Ted Shackley and was assigned to Operation Tilt. Key Question 10 asks whether he is the man tipping his hat in Dealey Plaza.

people.name: David Atlee Phillips
people.summary: Ran the propaganda side of the 1954 Guatemala coup, worked undercover in Cuba in 1959–60, and was involved in the Bay of Pigs and, with E. Howard Hunt, anti-Castro plotting. Alpha 66 founder Antonio Veciana said his CIA handler was "Maurice Bishop"; Phillips denied to the HSCA in 1978 that he used the name, but the cast document says the record suggests he did.

people.name: Antonio Veciana
people.summary: Founded the anti-Castro group Alpha 66, which had CIA support. In 1963 its raids on Soviet ships in Cuban ports, which the Kennedy administration opposed, led to his and other leaders' confinement in Florida. Said his handler "Bishop" worked with him on plans to kill Castro; later worked for a U.S. aid agency in Bolivia and was involved in another failed attempt on Castro in 1971.

people.name: William Harvey
people.summary: Former FBI agent who joined the CIA, served in Berlin with Ted Shackley, ran the "Executive Action" program for removing foreign leaders, and took part in the 1961 plot to poison Castro. Sent to Rome as station chief after anti-Cuba operations wound down in 1962.

people.name: John Roselli
people.summary: Capone-era mobster who became a power in Las Vegas and an associate of Santo Trafficante. Took part in the CIA–Mafia plots against Castro and told his lawyer Edward Morgan that Castro had sent sniper teams to kill Kennedy in retaliation (course thesis 5). Disappeared in July 1976 after testifying about the plots; his body was found in an oil drum in the sea off Florida.

people.name: Tony Varona
people.summary: Cuban anti-communist who worked with Frank Sturgis and the CIA, led the exile Cuban Revolutionary Council, had documented ties to Trafficante and Roselli, and was involved in several plots against Castro.

people.name: Richard Cain
people.role: Chicago police officer and mob associate
people.summary: Made member of the Chicago Outfit placed in the Chicago police by Sam Giancana. The cast document says Giancana assigned him to the Castro plot after meeting the CIA, and that he trained Cuban exiles from Mexico City. Murdered by masked gunmen in a Chicago restaurant in 1973.

people.name: Desmond FitzGerald
people.summary: OSS veteran who became chief of the CIA's Cuban Task Force in 1962, was personally involved in plots against Castro, and in 1965 became head of the Directorate of Plans. Died in 1967.

people.name: Richard Helms
people.role: CIA Deputy Director for Plans, later Director
people.summary: OSS veteran and senior CIA officer. After the assassination he oversaw the CIA's inquiry into Oswald; when its first investigator, John Whitten, learned the FBI had withheld information and called his initial lone-gunman finding irrelevant, Helms removed him from the case.

people.name: Manuel Artime
people.role: Exile leader, Bay of Pigs brigade
people.summary: Anti-communist Cuban close to Robert Kennedy, a leader of Brigade 2506 at the Bay of Pigs, captured and ransomed. Worked with Howard Hunt on Castro plots and in 1963, with CIA funds via Ted Shackley, built a 300-man force in Nicaragua for a second invasion that Johnson cancelled after the assassination.

people.name: Rafael "Chi Chi" Quintero
people.summary: Joined Artime's anti-Castro struggle, was part of Operation 40 and the Nicaragua operation, later worked on other CIA operations, and remained in covert work until his death in 2006. Named in Key Question 5.

people.name: Manuel Ray
people.summary: Castro's Minister of Public Works who broke with him and founded the MRP, joined the exile councils, then broke with the CIA after the Bay of Pigs and formed JURE in 1962, the group Sylvia Odio's visitors claimed to represent. Later moved his operations offshore and eventually to Puerto Rico.

people.name: Carlos Prío Socarrás
people.summary: Cuban president from 1948 until Batista's 1952 coup; financed Castro, then broke with him and went into exile in Miami. Testimony linked him with Jack Ruby and Frank Sturgis. Found shot dead outside his Miami home in 1977, the year the House committee wanted to question him.

people.name: Roy Hargraves
people.summary: Member of Gerry Patrick Hemming's Intercontinental Penetration Force (Interpen), trained exiles and led raids on Cuba with Felipe Vidal Santiago, including a plan to provoke war by staging an attack on Guantánamo. Died in 2002.

people.name: Felipe Vidal Santiago
people.summary: Former Cuban naval officer who joined Interpen raids, was close to John Martino and raised money for exile groups. The cast document says evidence suggests he was one of the shooters.

people.name: Bernardo de Torres
people.summary: Miami private investigator who was Brigade 2506's intelligence chief, captured and released in 1962. The cast document says he may have been one of Odio's two visitors, had CIA and Mafia ties, and was close to Oswald and the plot.

people.name: Loran Hall
people.summary: U.S. Army veteran who fought with Castro's rebels, fell out with him, then joined Sturgis's anti-communist brigade. Testified that Giancana put up $15,000 for the Operation Tilt raid and that he ran missions against Cuba for the CIA with Rip Robertson.

people.name: Frank Sturgis
people.summary: WWII Marine who worked with Castro's rebels, then the CIA. Formed an anti-communist brigade, flew leaflet raids over Cuba, took part in plots against Castro and Operation 40, and was arrested in the Watergate break-in. The cast document treats him as a key player in the assassination; Key Question 5 asks if he was in Dealey Plaza.

people.name: Bernard Barker
people.summary: Cuban-born U.S. veteran, later in Cuba's National Police, recruited by the FBI and then the CIA. Worked under Howard Hunt recruiting for Brigade 2506 and was one of the Watergate burglars.

people.name: E. Howard Hunt
people.summary: OSS veteran and CIA officer in the 1954 Guatemala coup and a planner of the Bay of Pigs; a key organizer of the Watergate burglary. Key Question 5 asks whether he was in Dealey Plaza.

people.name: Virgilio González
people.summary: Miami exile who went into Cuba on Operation Tilt and was a Watergate burglar. Named by John Martino as one of the gunmen; the cast document says evidence suggests his involvement.

people.name: Sergio Arcacha Smith
people.summary: Batista-era diplomat who led an anti-Castro front in New Orleans with David Ferrie, was pushed out in 1962 over missing funds, and resisted Jim Garrison's attempt to extradite him from Texas for questioning.

people.name: Emilio Santana
people.summary: Cuban fisherman recruited by the CIA to guide infiltration boats until he was dropped in October 1963. The cast document says evidence suggests his involvement.

people.name: David Ferrie
people.summary: Civil Air Patrol instructor who knew the teenage Oswald, was involved in anti-Castro plotting, and was a central figure in Garrison's case. Found dead in his apartment in February 1967, days after news broke that Garrison was investigating him.

people.name: Orest Peña
people.summary: Cuban owner of the Habana Bar in New Orleans, who said Oswald came in, argued about the price of a drink and complained about capitalism.

people.name: Tony Cuesta
people.summary: Helped found Alpha 66 and Commandos L and worked with Eddie Bayo. Captured on a 1966 raid, he lost an arm and his sight when he set off a grenade trying to kill himself. Released in 1978, he reportedly told Cuba's intelligence chief Fabián Escalante he had been involved in the assassination.

people.name: Herminio Díaz García
people.summary: Cuban gunman and bodyguard for Santo Trafficante, linked to assassination attempts abroad. Came to the U.S. in mid-1963 and worked with Tony Varona; named by John Martino as one of the gunmen. Killed on a 1966 raid into Cuba with Tony Cuesta.

people.name: Eladio del Valle
people.summary: Batista-era congressman who in Florida joined the Free Cuba Committee and worked with Trafficante and Ferrie on raids. Brutally murdered in Miami within hours of Ferrie's death in 1967; the cast document says witnesses tie him to the assassination.

people.name: Santo Trafficante Jr.
people.summary: Inherited his father's Florida and Havana rackets in 1954, took part in the CIA–Mafia plots against Castro and had ties to Jack Ruby. The cast document says a large body of evidence suggests he helped plan the assassination (course theses 3 and 6).

people.name: Lee Harvey Oswald
people.summary: In the Civil Air Patrol under David Ferrie as a teenager; Marine; defected to the USSR in 1959 (some argue as a CIA "dangle"), married Marina Prusakova and returned in 1962. In Texas he was befriended by Russian émigrés including George de Mohrenschildt. Accused of the April 1963 attempt on General Edwin Walker, of killing Officer J.D. Tippit, and of killing Kennedy; he was murdered by Jack Ruby two days later and never tried. The cast document argues much evidence cuts against his guilt as a lone gunman.

people.name: William Seymour
people.summary: Navy veteran and Interpen member who trained CIA-funded exile groups; thought by some to be one of Sylvia Odio's visitors.

people.name: Lawrence Howard
people.summary: Interpen member who worked with William Seymour, associated with David Ferrie in New Orleans; also suggested as one of Odio's visitors.

people.name: Ted Shackley
people.summary: Army counterintelligence, then CIA under William Harvey. Ran the Miami JM/WAVE station from 1962, gained control of Operation 40, organized Operation Tilt and continued plots against Castro. The cast document says evidence suggests he helped plan the assassination.

people.name: Allen Dulles
people.summary: From a family of secretaries of state, a Sullivan & Cromwell lawyer, OSS spymaster and a founder of the CIA, which he led under Eisenhower and Kennedy until Kennedy fired him after the Bay of Pigs. Johnson then appointed him to the Warren Commission.

groups.exile: Cuban exiles and soldiers of fortune
